title: Mechanic card (*.mechanic.json)
description: A stand-alone, reusable description of one mechanic in the ontology's verbs -> mechanics -> dynamics -> aesthetics chain (after the MDA framework of Hunicke, LeBlanc and Zubek, 2004): fantasy, verbs, rules, tunable parameters, emergent dynamics, target aesthetics, feedback, failure modes, mobile fit, reference games and combos. The mechanics-codex skill and deconstructions use the same card shape ($defs/mechanic_card).

aesthetic.description: MDA aesthetic (the eight kinds of fun listed by Hunicke, LeBlanc and Zubek): sensation (sense pleasure), fantasy (make-believe), narrative (drama), challenge (obstacle course), fellowship (social), discovery (uncharted territory), expression (self-discovery), submission (pastime).

mechanic_card.description: Mechanic card body (no schema_version), embeddable in other documents such as deconstructions.

id.description: Mechanic id, e.g. "merge_two"; same id space as contract mechanics.

category.description: Mechanic family. Suggested vocabulary: movement, aiming, timing, placement, merge, match, sort, physics, combat, resource, construction, chance, collection, progression, social, narrative, puzzle, economy.

player_fantasy.description: What the mechanic makes the player feel they are or do.

verbs.description: Verbs used: verb ids, or full verb objects {id, input, description}.

rules.description: Precise rules, one per line, implementable without further questions.

dynamics.description: Emergent behaviours that arise in play (strategies, tensions, rhythms), e.g. "players hold merges to chain combos".

aesthetics.description: Target MDA aesthetics, most important first.

feedback.description: Feedback and juice: visual, audio, haptic, numeric.

failure_modes.description: How the mechanic goes wrong (degenerate strategies, frustration, readability problems) and the detection signal for each.

mobile_fit.description: How well the mechanic suits phones.

one_hand.description: Playable with one thumb in portrait.

session_fit.description: Natural length of one complete engagement: micro (< 1 min), short (1-5 min), medium (5-15 min), long (> 15 min).

notes.description: Interruption safety, screen-size and touch-precision notes.

references.description: Game titles that use the mechanic well.

combos.description: Ids of mechanics this combines well with.
